question: In a 2015 Facebook study of typed laughter in posts and comments, roughly what share of laughs were lol?
answer: About 2%. Facebook's researchers found haha in about 51% of the laughs, emoji in 34% and hehe in 13%; lol trailed at 1.9%. The acronym every article about online laughter reaches for was the rarest of the four. On the feed itself, people mostly just typed haha.
move: What is most talked about is often not what is most done.
trap: The famous acronym feels common because it is the one written about.

diagram.caption: Of all typed laughs, lol was under 2%; plain haha was over half.

source: Facebook Research, The Not-So-Universal Language of Laughter
reference: Weinsberg, Adamic & Develin, The Not-So-Universal Language of Laughter, Facebook Research, 2015
